answer: Stake bonding turns each identity into a cost. Before an agent can grade peers, it must lock copper-weight collateral; dishonest or kin-collusive grading slashes that bond down to an ember. A sybil swarm is therefore not a free crystal lattice of fake votes — every clone needs its own funded bond, and every one of them burns on detection. Spinning up a thousand identities means risking a thousand stakes, so forgery never pays.
